title: Sieve of Eratosthenes
what: naive = stdlib DynamicArray<u8> (get/set under bounds proofs); optimized safe = safe dynarray with bounds proofs; optimized unsafe = unsafe dynarray, no checks. C, C++ and Rust: free = release memory at the end, leak = do not

caspien.label: Caspien naive (DynamicArray)
caspien.desc: stdlib DynamicArray<u8>, get/set under bounds proofs

caspien.label: Caspien optimized safe
caspien.desc: safe dynarray, bounds proofs

caspien.desc: unsafe dynarray, no checks

caspien.label: Caspien naive (String class)
caspien.desc: stdlib String: appendChar/charAt/setCharAt per character

caspien.label: Caspien optimized safe
caspien.desc: safe dynarray<u8> buffers, bounds proofs

caspien.label: Caspien optimized unsafe
caspien.desc: unsafe dynarray<u8> buffers, no checks

title: Heap graph search
what: N nodes on the heap with four edges each, find a needle by breadth-first search. The other languages allocate every node separately and link them with pointers; Caspien structs may only point at themselves through a plain nullable `ref`, so there are two families: INDEX edges (naive/optimized rows: parallel arrays, or one dynarray of Node structs in the struct-node rows) and REF rows, where every node is its own heap object with four `ref` edges to other nodes, each node access under a ghost-table alive proof

caspien.label: Caspien naive (DynamicArray)
caspien.desc: stdlib DynamicArray<u64> x4 (index-based edges), get/set under bounds proofs

caspien.label: Caspien optimized safe
caspien.desc: safe dynarrays, bounds proofs

caspien.label: Caspien optimized unsafe
caspien.desc: unsafe dynarrays, no checks

caspien.label: Caspien struct nodes, safe
caspien.desc: ONE safe dynarray of Node structs (value, dist, 4 edge indices), bounds proofs

caspien.label: Caspien struct nodes, unsafe
caspien.desc: ONE unsafe dynarray of Node structs, no checks

caspien.label: Caspien ref naive
caspien.desc: REF: every node its own heap object, 4 plain `ref` edges to nodes of the same struct, owned by a dynarray of owns slots; BFS queue = stdlib DynamicArray<QRef>; alive proof per deref

caspien.label: Caspien ref safe
caspien.desc: REF: self-referential Node (4 `ref` edges), owner dynarray + queue of refs in safe dynarrays, alive proof per deref

caspien.label: Caspien ref unsafe
caspien.desc: REF: as ref safe, but the queue of refs is an unsafe dynarray (the owner dynarray must stay safe)

title: Sorting and searching
what: quicksort, merge sort and heap sort of N random values, N binary searches and 20 linear searches. Caspien elements are u64 (the others use 32-bit ints)

caspien.label: Caspien naive (DynamicArray)
caspien.desc: stdlib DynamicArray<u64>, get/set under bounds proofs

caspien.label: Caspien optimized safe
caspien.desc: safe dynarrays, bounds proofs

caspien.label: Caspien optimized unsafe
caspien.desc: unsafe dynarrays, no checks

title: Binary trees
what: allocate, walk and free many complete binary trees (a stretch tree, one long-lived tree, then 2^(N-d+4) trees of each depth d = 4, 6, .., N). The other languages use pointer nodes; Caspien has two families: an index-based tree (children are indices, 0 = null) in a dynarray of Node structs with a free list and an explicit work stack (naive uses one stdlib DynamicArray<Node>: get plus the pointer-taking setPtr), and the REF rows, where every node is a real heap object whose l/r are plain `ref` members of the same struct (alive proof per deref, owned by a pool of owns slots)

caspien.label: Caspien naive (DynamicArray)
caspien.desc: index-based tree: ONE stdlib DynamicArray<Node> pool + DynamicArray<u64> work stack, free-list pool, get/setPtr under bounds proofs

caspien.label: Caspien optimized safe
caspien.desc: index-based tree: ONE safe dynarray of Node structs (l, r indices) + free list, bounds proofs

caspien.label: Caspien optimized unsafe
caspien.desc: index-based tree: ONE unsafe dynarray of Node structs + free list, no checks

caspien.label: Caspien ref naive
caspien.desc: REF: every node its own heap object (new Node) with `ref` l/r members of the same struct, owned by a pool of owns slots; stacks = stdlib DynamicArray; alive proof per deref

caspien.label: Caspien ref safe
caspien.desc: REF: self-referential Node, owner pool + stacks in safe dynarrays, alive proof per deref

caspien.label: Caspien ref unsafe
caspien.desc: REF: as ref safe, with unsafe dynarray work stacks (the owner pool must stay safe)

title: Mandelbrot
what: escape-time count over an N x N grid, at most 100 iterations per point; f64 scalar maths, no arrays or allocation (a single Caspien variant)

caspien.label: Caspien f64 scalars
caspien.desc: f64 scalar maths, no arrays or allocation (loop indices mirrored as f64, no int-to-float cast)

title: FASTA generation
what: LCG-driven repeat and weighted random sequences written into one heap buffer; prints length, checksum and letter counts (integer thresholds, no floating point)

caspien.label: Caspien naive (DynamicArray)
caspien.desc: stdlib DynamicArray<u8>/<u64> for the output buffer, constant table and thresholds, get/set under bounds proofs

caspien.label: Caspien optimized safe
caspien.desc: safe dynarrays, bounds proofs

caspien.label: Caspien optimized unsafe
caspien.desc: unsafe dynarrays, no checks

title: k-nucleotide (hash map)
what: count k-mer frequencies for k = 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12 in a generated DNA sequence. C and the optimized Caspien variants use a hand-written open-addressing table; the other languages use their idiomatic maps; Caspien naive uses the stdlib HashMap. The LCG period is 139,968, so the tables stay small and cache-friendly

caspien.label: Caspien naive (stdlib HashMap)
caspien.desc: stdlib HashMap<u64> (insecure_hashOf per key, fixed capacity) + DynamicArray, get/set under bounds proofs

caspien.label: Caspien optimized safe
caspien.desc: hand-written open-addressing table in safe dynarrays, bounds proofs

caspien.label: Caspien optimized unsafe
caspien.desc: hand-written open-addressing table in unsafe dynarrays, no checks

caspien.label: Caspien naive, ref in stdlib
caspien.desc: identical to naive, but the stdlib HashMap is stdlib/ref/hash_map.caspien (separate chaining over `ref` nodes)

title: LRU cache
what: capacity 262,144 over 1,048,576 keys, 75% of operations on a hot subset, hash map plus recency list. Optimized Caspien: index-based doubly linked list and chained hash map in dynarrays; naive: stdlib DynamicArray + HashMap (no remove, evicted keys map to a sentinel)

caspien.label: Caspien naive (DynamicArray + HashMap)
caspien.desc: stdlib DynamicArray<u64> node pool + stdlib HashMap<u64> (key -> node index; no remove, evicted keys map to a NONE sentinel), get/set under bounds proofs

caspien.label: Caspien optimized safe
caspien.desc: safe dynarrays: index-based doubly linked recency list + chained hash map threaded through the node pool, bounds proofs

caspien.label: Caspien optimized unsafe
caspien.desc: unsafe dynarrays, same index-based list and chained hash map, no checks

caspien.label: Caspien ref naive
caspien.desc: REF: doubly linked list + hash chains of heap Entry nodes with `ref` prv/nxt/hn members; bucket heads in a stdlib DynamicArray<QRef>; alive proof per deref

caspien.label: Caspien ref safe
caspien.desc: REF: self-referential Entry (prv/nxt/hn refs), owner pool + bucket heads in safe dynarrays

caspien.label: Caspien ref unsafe
caspien.desc: REF: as ref safe, bucket heads in an unsafe dynarray

caspien.label: Caspien naive, ref in stdlib
caspien.desc: identical to naive, but the stdlib HashMap is stdlib/ref/hash_map.caspien (separate chaining over `ref` nodes)

title: Merkle tree
what: build a Merkle tree over N leaves, then generate and verify N/2 proofs (every 4th tampered). The hash is real SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4, hand-written in every language, no crypto library): one compression per leaf, two per internal node

caspien.label: Caspien naive (DynamicArray)
caspien.desc: real SHA-256; stdlib DynamicArray<u32> x3 (leaf data, flat tree of 8-word digests, proof path), get/set under bounds proofs

caspien.label: Caspien optimized safe
caspien.desc: real SHA-256; safe dynarrays, bounds proofs

caspien.label: Caspien optimized unsafe
caspien.desc: real SHA-256; unsafe dynarrays, no checks

title: Hello World
what: print one line: measures start-up time, compile time and binary size

caspien.label: Caspien plain printf
caspien.desc: single printf of the line, no allocation (N ignored); measures startup, compile time and binary size

title: JSON serialise + parse
what: hand-written serialiser writes N records to one text buffer, a hand-written iterative parser reads them back; every language does the same work (no JSON library). Naive keeps the records in one stdlib DynamicArray<Rec>

caspien.label: Caspien naive (DynamicArray)
caspien.desc: stdlib DynamicArray<u8> buffers + ONE DynamicArray<Rec> for the records, get/setPtr under bounds proofs

caspien.label: Caspien optimized safe
caspien.desc: safe dynarrays (u8 buffers + one dynarray of Rec structs), bounds proofs

caspien.label: Caspien optimized unsafe
caspien.desc: unsafe dynarrays (u8 buffers + one dynarray of Rec structs), no checks

title: Thread spawn
what: N tasks (a multiple of 64) run in waves of 64 OS threads, each thread runs the same integer kernel on its own state and the results are added up after the join. No data is shared between threads. Only languages with OS-level threads are included.

caspien.label: Caspien naive
caspien.desc: the kernel step is a function call

caspien.label: Caspien optimized
caspien.desc: kernel inlined by hand and unrolled four times

title: Swap lock contention
what: 32 OS threads each update one shared (count, sum) struct N times under one lock (Caspien: a swap lock; the others: their standard mutex). The result does not depend on the order of the updates.

caspien.label: Caspien naive
caspien.desc: a CLOSED lock is retried at once (pure spinning)

caspien.label: Caspien optimized
caspien.desc: a backoff policy yields the time slice every 16th failed attempt
